dc:title: PLATO spreadsheet tables
dc:description: CSV on the Web (CSVW) metadata for organising data about places in PLATO's shape with spreadsheets. It describes ten linked tables, how they refer to one another, and how each row becomes RDF in the PLATO ontology (https://w3id.org/plato#). Keep every table, even if you leave it empty apart from its header row. The published addresses (IRIs) of a dataset made from these tables are normative, and PLATO tools makes them: the base is the one given for a conversion, if any, else about's base_uri, with a '/' added when it ends in neither '/' nor '#'; the dataset (the plato:Gazetteer) is named by about's dataset_uri, or by that base when dataset_uri is empty; each place is <base>place/<place_id> and each source <base>source/<source_id>, with every character of the identifier other than the RFC 3986 unreserved characters (A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~) percent-encoded as UTF-8, so that ! ' ( ) * are encoded too (identifiers SHOULD use unreserved characters only); every other node (each attestation, and its name, location, date and citation) has no address of its own. CSVW cannot build an address from a cell of another table, so converting the tables with a CSVW processor alone gives the places, sources and rows addresses relative to their CSV files (places.csv#bristol), and names the dataset about.csv itself when dataset_uri is empty, since a URI template has no fallback value: that graph is for validating the tables, and its addresses are not the dataset's. Guide: https://pelagios.org/place-attestation-ontology/guide/.

tables.dc:title: About
tables.dc:description: One row describing the dataset as a whole: its title, who made it, its licence, what it covers, and the base of its web addresses. It is what makes the dataset findable and citable (the FAIR principles). Exactly one row. Only the title is required, and the licence too once status is 'published'. The creator_name column is deprecated: names go in creator, which takes a name, a web address, or a name with its address.

columns.name: title
columns.dc:description: The dataset's title.

columns.name: description
columns.dc:description: What the dataset is, in a sentence or two: where it comes from and what it covers. Optional.

columns.name: creator
columns.dc:description: The people or organisations to cite as its authors, separated by ';'. Write each as a name and its web address together, the address in angle brackets (Josiah Carberry <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097>), or as a web address alone, or as a name alone. Optional; give an ORCID where you can. In the tables each author is recorded as text, as written; converting with PLATO tools turns the address into a link and gives it the name.

columns.name: creator_name
columns.dc:description: Deprecated: write these names in creator instead, which now takes a name alone as well as a name with its address. The names of authors who have no web address, separated by ';'. Optional. Kept for one release, and to be withdrawn after it.

columns.name: contributor
columns.dc:description: The web address of the person or organisation that owns or maintains the dataset, if not its author. Optional.

columns.name: licence
columns.dc:description: The web address of the dataset's licence, such as https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Required once status is 'published'.

columns.name: version
columns.dc:description: The dataset's version, in any form you use: '1.2', '2026-09'. Optional.

columns.name: status
columns.dc:description: 'draft' while it may still change, or 'published' once others may cite it. Once published, its evidence is only ever added to, never changed. Optional.

columns.name: keywords
columns.dc:description: Words a catalogue can find it by, separated by ';'. Optional.

columns.name: spatial
columns.dc:description: The area it covers, as web addresses (a Wikidata or GeoNames region), separated by ';'. Optional. In the tables these are recorded as web addresses in text form; converting with PLATO tools turns them into links.

columns.name: temporal_from
columns.dc:description: The earliest year or date the dataset covers, with at least four digits. Optional.

columns.name: temporal_to
columns.dc:description: The latest year or date it covers, in the same form. Optional.

columns.name: landing_page
columns.dc:description: The web page where people find and download the dataset. Optional.

columns.name: dataset_uri
columns.dc:description: The dataset's own permanent web address, if it has one: the address that names the dataset itself when it is converted. Optional; if it is empty, the dataset is named by the base of its addresses (base_uri).

columns.name: base_uri
columns.dc:description: The base of the web addresses of the dataset's places and sources, such as https://w3id.org/my-project/: choose one you control and will keep. Each place's address is this base, then place/, then its place_id (https://w3id.org/my-project/place/bristol), and each source's is the base, then source/, then its source_id. Use only letters, digits and - . _ ~ in the identifiers, or they are percent-encoded in the address. A base given when converting (in PLATO tools, 'Web address for your identifiers') is used instead of this one. Optional, but give it before publishing: without it the addresses are not permanent.

tables.dc:title: Places
tables.dc:description: One row per place, or other spatial entity, that your data is about: a settlement, a region, a river, a road, an administrative unit. Each row becomes a plato:SpatialEntity. Everything else about a place (its names, locations, types) goes in the other sheets, where it can carry a date and a source.

columns.name: place_id
columns.dc:description: A short identifier for the place, unique in this sheet. Use letters, digits and - . _ ~ only ('bristol', 'p1'): any other character is percent-encoded in the place's web address. The other sheets use it to refer to this row. It is also kept in the data as the place's identifier, so a record can be traced back to your row, and it ends the place's web address: the about sheet's base_uri, then place/, then this (https://w3id.org/my-project/place/bristol), or the base given when converting, if one is. So keep it once the dataset is published.

columns.name: label
columns.dc:description: The name you want the place to be listed under. This is a display label only: the names the place has in your sources go in the names sheet.

columns.name: country_codes
columns.dc:description: Two-letter ISO codes of the modern countries whose territory contains or overlaps the place, separated by ';'. A finding aid for search and matching, not evidence. Optional.

tables.dc:title: Sources
tables.dc:description: One row per source you cite: a document, a map, a book, a dataset. Each row becomes a plato:Source. Every row in the attestation sheets names one of these in its source_id column.

columns.name: source_id
columns.dc:description: A short identifier for the source, unique in this sheet ('domesday', 's1'), in letters, digits and - . _ ~ only: any other character is percent-encoded in the address. It ends the source's web address: the about sheet's base_uri (or the base given when converting), then source/, then this (https://w3id.org/my-project/source/domesday). So keep it once the dataset is published.

columns.name: title
columns.dc:description: A short title for the source, as you would refer to it ('Domesday Book').

columns.name: citation
columns.dc:description: A full bibliographic citation, in any style. Optional.

columns.name: uri
columns.dc:description: A web address for the source, if it has one. Optional.

columns.name: date
columns.dc:description: When the source itself was made: written, copied, printed or published, as the source or catalogue gives it. Write 'undated' if unknown. Required.

columns.name: from
columns.dc:description: Earliest year or date the source can have been made, with at least four digits, or YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

columns.name: to
columns.dc:description: Latest year or date the source can have been made. Optional.

columns.name: derived_from
columns.dc:description: If this source is a copy, transcript or edition of another source in this sheet, that source's source_id. Optional.

columns.name: licence
columns.dc:description: The web address of the licence of the source as you cite it (the edition or copy), for example https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Optional.

tables.dc:title: Names
tables.dc:description: One row for each time a source gives a name for a place. Each row becomes a plato:Attestation of one plato:Name, with its date and source.

columns.name: place_id
columns.dc:description: The place this row is about: a place_id from the places sheet.

columns.name: name
columns.dc:description: The name, spelt exactly as the source gives it.

columns.name: language
columns.dc:description: The language of the name, as a language code ('en', 'la', 'enm' for Middle English). Optional.

columns.name: script
columns.dc:description: The writing system, as a four-letter code ('Latn', 'Arab', 'Grek'). Optional.

columns.name: romanized
columns.dc:description: The name in Latin letters, if the source uses another script. Optional.

columns.name: name_type
columns.dc:description: What the name names, if not a place: 'toponym' (the default), 'hydronym' (a river or lake), 'odonym' (a street), 'ethnonym', 'demonym', 'chrononym'. Several may be separated by ';'. Optional.

columns.name: form_status
columns.dc:description: What kind of form this is: 'Attested' (read in the source; the default), 'Headword' (the form an editor files the entry under), 'Normalised' (a spelling made up for searching), 'Reconstructed' (inferred, not found), 'Preferred' (the form your project prefers for display and search, which the source may not show), 'Editorial' (written by the editors of the edition you cite, in their commentary or notes, not in the text they edit). Leave empty for an ordinary reading.

columns.name: occurrence_context
columns.dc:description: How the name occurs: 'InPersonalName' if it appears only inside a person's name ('Willelmus de Bonestou'), 'InFieldName' if only inside a later minor name. Leave empty for an ordinary mention.

columns.name: occurrence_count
columns.dc:description: How many times the name occurs in the passage cited, if more than once. Optional.

columns.name: transcription_accuracy
columns.dc:description: How faithfully the name renders what the source shows: 'Accurate', 'Inaccurate' (misread), or 'False' (a ghost form not in the source). Optional.

columns.name: transcription_completeness
columns.dc:description: Whether the name is whole: 'Complete', 'Reconstructable' (part lost, but it can be supplied), or 'NonReconstructable'. Optional.

columns.name: date
columns.dc:description: The date as your source gives it, in any form: '1086', 'c. 925', '1480-1485', 'a. 1300'. Write 'undated' if the source gives no date. Required on every row.

columns.name: from
columns.dc:description: Earliest year or date the row can refer to, with at least four digits (0921, not 921; -12000 for 12,000 BCE) or YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; leave empty if you cannot say.

columns.name: to
columns.dc:description: Latest year or date the row can refer to, in the same form as 'from'. For a single year, put it in both 'from' and 'to'. Leave empty if the end is unknown.

columns.name: source_id
columns.dc:description: The source this comes from: a source_id from the sources sheet.

columns.name: locator
columns.dc:description: Where in the source: a page, folio, column or entry, written as the source numbers it ('p. 25', 'f. 12v'). Optional.

columns.name: attribution
columns.dc:description: 'Inferred' if the source was given as 'ibid.' or 'idem' and an editor worked out which source was meant. Leave empty otherwise.

columns.name: citation_function
columns.dc:description: Why the source is cited, as a term of CiTO, the Citation Typing Ontology: 'citesAsEvidence' (the source is the evidence), 'citesAsDataSource', 'citesAsRelated', 'citesForInformation' and so on. Optional; leave empty if your data does not say.

columns.name: certainty
columns.dc:description: How sure you are of this row, from 0 (not at all) to 1 (certain). Optional: if your source or your judgement gives certainty in words, use certainty_level instead, rather than inventing a number.

columns.name: certainty_level
columns.dc:description: Certainty in words: 'Certain', 'LessCertain' or 'Uncertain', the three levels of Linked Places Format. Optional; may be given with or instead of certainty.

columns.name: denied
columns.dc:description: 'yes' if the source says this is not so: no market here, a grant refused. The row then records a denial, not an assertion, so give only the one thing the source denies. Leave empty for an ordinary row.

columns.name: stance
columns.dc:description: How firmly the source itself says it: 'Reported' if the source passes it on without vouching for it ('it is said'), 'Tentative' if it hedges, 'Doubted' if it raises it but will not decide (that is not a denial: use denied for that), or 'Asserted'. Leave empty where the source simply states it. This is the source's stance, not how sure you are, which is certainty.

columns.name: notes
columns.dc:description: Anything else worth saying about this row, in your own words. Optional.

columns.name: latitude
columns.dc:description: Latitude in decimal degrees, WGS 84 (as in most web maps).

columns.name: longitude
columns.dc:description: Longitude in decimal degrees, WGS 84. West of Greenwich is negative.

columns.name: wkt
columns.dc:description: A shape (line or polygon) as Well-Known Text, if you have one. Optional.

columns.name: geometry_role
columns.dc:description: What the location marks: 'Extent' (the whole place), 'FeaturePoint' (a particular feature, such as the church), 'RepresentativePoint' (a point standing in for the place, as a symbol on a map usually is), 'LabelAnchor', 'Itinerary'. Optional.

columns.name: precision_km
columns.dc:description: How far out the location might be, in kilometres. Optional.

columns.name: type_label

For an OpenStreetMap tag, include its key (https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:waterway=stream). Leave it empty for a category of your source's own that no vocabulary holds. Optional.

columns.name: type_scheme
columns.dc:description: The web address of the vocabulary the type comes from, if type_uri does not already make it plain: for Köppen codes, WWF ecoregions or your project's own list. Optional.

columns.name: type_scheme_version

tables.dc:title: Relations
tables.dc:description: One row for each time a source relates a place to something else: a parish lying in a hundred, a station on a road, a stop on a journey, one place leading to another, a place where a person was born. Each row becomes a plato:Attestation relating the place in place_id either to another place, in related_place_id, or to something described elsewhere (a person, an object, an event), in related_uri. Fill in exactly one of the two: CSVW cannot state that rule, so PLATO tools checks it.

columns.name: place_id
columns.dc:description: The place this row is about: a place_id from the places sheet.

columns.name: relation_type
columns.dc:description: How they are related. Places within places: 'ContainedIn' (the place in place_id lies within the other). Routes, journeys and networks: 'MemberOf' (the place is a station, stop or member of the route, journey or network in related_place_id; give its position in sequence), 'ConnectedTo' (directly connected, either way), 'LeadsTo' (connected one way, from place_id to the other), 'BeginsAt' and 'EndsAt' (a segment, such as a leg of a road, begins or ends at the other place), 'HasEnd' (the other place is one end of a segment with no direction; give it for both ends). People, objects and events, in related_uri: 'BirthplaceOf', 'DeathplaceOf', 'ResidenceOf', 'FindspotOf', 'SettingOf', 'WorkplaceOf'. Images and records about a place, in related_uri: 'DepictedIn' (a photograph, map or drawing shows it), 'SubjectOf' (an archival file, report or publication is about it). Only PLATO's own relation types can be used here; a project's own (declared in JSON or RDF with broader_relation) cannot, and further types are added to PLATO's vocabulary on request.

columns.name: related_place_id
columns.dc:description: The other place: a place_id from the places sheet. Leave empty if the row relates the place to something that is not a place, in related_uri.

columns.name: related_uri
columns.dc:description: The web address of what the place is related to, when it is not a place in your places sheet: a person, an object or an event described elsewhere, such as http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q9441 for the Buddha. Leave empty if you filled in related_place_id.

columns.name: related_label
columns.dc:description: A name for what related_uri points to ('the Buddha'), so that it can be shown without looking the address up. Give it whenever you fill in related_uri.

columns.name: sequence
columns.dc:description: For MemberOf: the place's position on the route or journey, as your source orders it (1, 2, 3 ...). Two places with the same number are alternatives. Leave empty if the source gives no order.

columns.name: date
columns.dc:description: The date as your source gives it, in any form: '1086', 'c. 925', '1480-1485', 'a. 1300'. Write 'undated' if the source gives no date. Required on every row.

tables.dc:title: Connections
tables.dc:description: One row for each figure a source gives about a connection between two places: the number of letters sent from one city to another, a journey time, a toll, a cargo. Each row becomes a plato:Attestation relating the place in place_id to the place in related_place_id, with one plato:PropertyValue. Several figures about one connection are several rows. A connection with no figures goes in the relations sheet; a physical link with its own existence, such as a leg of a road, is better entered as a place of its own, with its figures in the properties sheet.

columns.dc:description: The place this row is about: a place_id from the places sheet.

columns.name: relation_type

columns.dc:description: Certainty in words: 'Certain', 'LessCertain' or 'Uncertain', the three levels of Linked Places Format. Optional; may be given with or instead of certainty.

columns.name: denied
columns.dc:description: 'yes' if the source says this is not so: no market here, a grant refused. The row then records a denial, not an assertion, so give only the one thing the source denies. Leave empty for an ordinary row.

columns.name: stance
columns.dc:description: How firmly the source itself says it: 'Reported' if the source passes it on without vouching for it ('it is said'), 'Tentative' if it hedges, 'Doubted' if it raises it but will not decide (that is not a denial: use denied for that), or 'Asserted'. Leave empty where the source simply states it. This is the source's stance, not how sure you are, which is certainty.

columns.name: notes
columns.dc:description: Anything else worth saying about this row, in your own words. Optional.

tables.dc:title: Properties
tables.dc:description: One row for each other fact a source states about a place: a population, a valuation, a market day. Each row becomes a plato:Attestation of one plato:PropertyValue. A latitude given without a longitude is a property too, not a location: property_uri http://www.w3.org/2003/01/geo/wgs84_pos#lat, with the value in decimal degrees.

columns.name: place_id
columns.dc:description: The place this row is about: a place_id from the places sheet.

columns.name: property_uri
columns.dc:description: What is being stated, as the web address of a property in a published vocabulary, for example Wikidata's 'population'.

columns.name: property_label
columns.dc:description: What is being stated, in words ('population'). Optional.

columns.name: value
columns.dc:description: The value, as the source gives it or as a number.

columns.name: unit_uri
columns.dc:description: The unit, as the web address of a unit in a published vocabulary, if the value has one. Optional.

columns.name: date
columns.dc:description: The date as your source gives it, in any form: '1086', 'c. 925', '1480-1485', 'a. 1300'. Write 'undated' if the source gives no date. Required on every row.

columns.name: from
columns.dc:description: Earliest year or date the row can refer to, with at least four digits (0921, not 921; -12000 for 12,000 BCE) or YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; leave empty if you cannot say.

columns.name: to
columns.dc:description: Latest year or date the row can refer to, in the same form as 'from'. For a single year, put it in both 'from' and 'to'. Leave empty if the end is unknown.

columns.name: source_id
columns.dc:description: The source this comes from: a source_id from the sources sheet.

columns.name: locator
columns.dc:description: Where in the source: a page, folio, column or entry, written as the source numbers it ('p. 25', 'f. 12v'). Optional.

columns.name: attribution
columns.dc:description: 'Inferred' if the source was given as 'ibid.' or 'idem' and an editor worked out which source was meant. Leave empty otherwise.

columns.name: citation_function
columns.dc:description: Why the source is cited, as a term of CiTO, the Citation Typing Ontology: 'citesAsEvidence' (the source is the evidence), 'citesAsDataSource', 'citesAsRelated', 'citesForInformation' and so on. Optional; leave empty if your data does not say.

columns.name: certainty
columns.dc:description: How sure you are of this row, from 0 (not at all) to 1 (certain). Optional: if your source or your judgement gives certainty in words, use certainty_level instead, rather than inventing a number.

columns.name: certainty_level
columns.dc:description: Certainty in words: 'Certain', 'LessCertain' or 'Uncertain', the three levels of Linked Places Format. Optional; may be given with or instead of certainty.

columns.name: denied
columns.dc:description: 'yes' if the source says this is not so: no market here, a grant refused. The row then records a denial, not an assertion, so give only the one thing the source denies. Leave empty for an ordinary row.

columns.name: stance
columns.dc:description: How firmly the source itself says it: 'Reported' if the source passes it on without vouching for it ('it is said'), 'Tentative' if it hedges, 'Doubted' if it raises it but will not decide (that is not a denial: use denied for that), or 'Asserted'. Leave empty where the source simply states it. This is the source's stance, not how sure you are, which is certainty.

columns.name: notes
columns.dc:description: Anything else worth saying about this row, in your own words. Optional.

tables.dc:title: Identities
tables.dc:description: One row for each record elsewhere (GeoNames, Wikidata, the World Historical Gazetteer, another dataset) that you believe is the same place as one of yours. Each row becomes a plato:IdentityRelation.

columns.name: place_id
columns.dc:description: Your place: a place_id from the places sheet.

columns.name: same_as
columns.dc:description: The web address of the other record.

columns.name: match_type
columns.dc:description: 'exactMatch' (certainly the same), 'closeMatch' (the same, with some difference of extent or scope), 'related' (closely associated), or 'unspecified' (your source links the two but does not say how strongly). Required, so that a match of unstated strength is marked as such rather than read as exact.

columns.name: certainty
columns.dc:description: How sure you are that they are the same, from 0 to 1. Optional.

columns.name: basis
columns.dc:description: Why you think so, in your own words. Optional.
columns.skos:example: Same name and position; the only plausible match.

columns.name: source_id
columns.dc:description: A source that supports the match, from the sources sheet. Optional.
